zh: 從標高3275公尺的武嶺 ( 台灣高山公路最高點 )，走下合歡山莊，山路平坦曲折，空氣稀薄清涼。左側的玉山箭竹揮灑一片，鋪綴著山坡成耀眼的橘黃地毯。疏落的台灣冷杉堅韌地聳立其上。南湖大山和中央尖山在北方天際遙遙相望。更遠處，想必是大甲溪和蘭陽溪千年侵奪的思源埡口吧！右側的合歡山壁，層岩疊錯，肌理似畫，削壁積雪叢叢，滴成涓涓細流。奇萊山和能高山在東南天邊綿延，在雲霧飄渺中，成嶺成脈。
en: From Wuling, at an elevation of 3,275 meters (the highest point on Taiwan's high mountain roads), descending toward Hehuan Mountain Lodge, the mountain road winds gently, the air thin and cool. To the left, Yushan cane spreads in a sweep, draping the slopes in a dazzling carpet of orange-yellow. Scattered Taiwan firs stand tenaciously above it. Nanhu Mountain and Zhongyangjian Mountain gaze at each other across the northern sky. Farther still must be Siyuan Pass, worn away over a thousand years by the Dajia and Lanyang Rivers! To the right, the cliffs of Hehuan Mountain rise in layered, folded rock, their texture like a painting, clusters of snow clinging to the sheer walls and dripping into thin trickling streams. Qilai Mountain and Nenggao Mountain stretch along the southeastern horizon, forming ridges and ranges amid drifting mist and cloud.

zh: 阿爾卑斯山的峻嶺雪峰
這裡呈現著獨特的景象
en: No need to tell me
The towering ridges and snow peaks of the Alps
The mist, haze, and cloud of Huangshan
Here a singular scene unfolds
Breathtakingly beautiful mountain scenery

zh: 便擁有這片蔚藍的天空
獨自展示著秀麗的風景
en: The mottled water-layered rock as witness
The floating white cloud as witness
From the depths of the sea
Rising to a height of 3,000 meters
For a million years
This beautiful island
Then possesses this stretch of azure sky
Displaying alone its graceful scenery

zh: 是我出世 e 所在，祖先e開墾
寶貴 e 文化，咱Tioh愛繼續
Koh  Kah伊保存落去，你 e 歷史Kap
自然 e 美，咱 be 永遠記住心內。”
en: A light breeze brushes the Yushan cane
Stammering into a tune:
"Those mountains there, that lake there, those fields there
It is where I was born, where my ancestors broke the land
This precious culture, we must continue on
Koh-kah, preserve it -- your history and
Nature's beauty -- let us keep it in our hearts forever.

points.zh: 陳芳玉女士所作「Chih把土」合唱曲的歌詞。
points.en: Lyrics of the choral piece "Grasp the Soil" (Chih Ba Tu), composed by Ms. Chen Fang-yu.
